Regular Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT
REGULAR
MEETING
WEDNESDAY, MAY 9, 2007
6:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and on the web at www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us .

Mayor Heebner presented the Proclamation proclaiming May 7-13 Public Service Week.

San Elijo JPA
Council and Mr. Thornton, San Elijo JPA, discussed the "Plant of the Year" award received by the JPA, the participation of ownership by Encinitas and Solana Beach, that ocean outfall is split with other cities and areas as owning part of the outfall, that the agency must comply with 36 permits, and that tours of the plant are available, that the Coastal Rail Trail has the local pipes ready for recyled water but the infrastructure is not built to deliver it yet, that the financial cost is $1,000,000 a mile, and that their financials are very secure and in time the members agencies would begin to receive reimbursement.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today's agenda by submitting a speaker slip to the City Clerk (located on the back table). Comments relating to items on this evening's agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Items can be referred to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES as per SBMC . (Be aware of the timer lights on the Council dais.)
Cassy Blacet, County Fair representative, announced that the fair begins June 8th and the theme is "Salute to Heroes" and that each day will have a more specific theme as well. She presented a powerpoint presentation highlighting the event and the parking.
Danny Hernandez said that he was unhappy with the community meeting with the Sheriff’s department at La Colonia Park, that residents tried to talk to them about the issues but that they gave the same answers without explanations, that it seemed like they were unwilling to work with the residents, that they made this community seem like it was the slum just because it is more blue collared in order to justify the policies they use against the children in this area, and that he asked Council to address these issues.
Robert Hernandez said that the residents of Eden Gardens are not proud or happy with the graffiti in park or on the fences, that this meeting was about graffiti and not about the issues that residents came to discuss which was the taking of photos of their children, that all the children are under 13 years old and they are scared now after their interaction iwth the Sheriffs, that he knows these kids and they are good kids who play play pool and wrestle in his back yard, and that he has asked them to find out who is doing the graffiti but that it is usually from Encinitas groups.
Councilmember Roberts asked what the next steps would be.
Mayor Heebner said that since it is oral communications it can not be addressed at this time as well as the issue is under investigation. She said that there are two opportnities for residents including a Citizen Academy and a Parent Youth Workshop on June 7th.
David Ott, City Manager, said that the Captain will present a comprehensive plan to him shortly, confirmed the open communication effort with the upcoming Citizen’s Academy and workshops.
Mayor Heebner stated that there were workshops and a committee that residents joined in developing the La Colonia Assessment Needs Plan and maybe cut down on graffiti.
Councilmember Roberts suggested that organizing the neighborhood watch program would help these concerns and a neighborhood can get help with it from the Sheriff's department.
Manny Rincon said that he was born and raised here and his family has Tony Zacals, that they have worked with the City over time, that he was at the meeting and like some of what was said and did not like other, he said that in the past Eden Gardens benefitted from the help of Council and the Sheriffs who did a lot to clean up and get rid of the those who caused problems, that the Encinitas troublemakers do not come around much, that they want the Sheriff around, but that some tactics should be reviewed, that it seemed like some law enforcement may be acting on misinformation or making conclusions too fast before knowing all the information, and that the overall problems are vandalism and graffiti.
Rose Hernandez said that her son had his photo taken and upset him, that he is now terrified to walk to Rudy’s, that she does not want her son to be afraid of police, that she wants the police around but not taking pictures of children, that they meet at the park on Wednesdays to go to church and his picture was taken and that he was told it was just for future use, that she did not want her son labeled as a gang member when he was just waiting to meet her and go to church, and that she signed up for the committee.
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Mayor Heebner announced that Bike to Work Day is May 18th, that the Trainstation meeting woudl be on June 14th. and that the May 10th meeting was cancelled, that a Council Meeting on the City budget was scheduled for May 30th.
Councilmember Roberts announced that the Civic and Historical Society would have a meeting this Friday at Fletcher Cove, that San Elijo Lagoon Day was this Saturday, that the Arts Alive Banner Auction put on by the Public Arts Advisory Commission was coming up, and that the new Fletcher Cove park would open on Memorial Day and that a ribbon cutting ceremony would be on June 16th.
COMMENTARY:
Deputy Mayor Kellejian asked that the Sheriffs drive through Solana Beach on their way back to the station rather than returning by the freeway.
Councilmember Roberts said that someone bought a roll of stamps at the post office and accidently left 40 rolls on the counter and someone turned them into the postal employees to return them to the owner.
David Ott, City Manager, announced that there is a tentative special meeting, not a Council meeting, for the Santa Fe Christian public workshop next Wednesday that will be held at City Hall before the June 16th potential request to Council.

6.

A. Adopt Resolution 2007-054
1.
Authorizing the City Manager to sign an agreement with Austin Foust & Associates, Inc. in the amount of $36,500 to be paid from a deposit from Shea Properties, Account 001-214.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item and reviewed past meetings, that a combined matrix consisting of questions from Council and information from a memo from Mr. Brohard, a traffic engineer used by some residents for some analysis, was passed out to Council. He said that Council had asked staff to locate a fourth party review traffic engineer with less ties to San Diego Council, NCTD and Sandag. He said he has been in close contact with Austin Foust, the responding firm agreeing to some deadlines, to provide specific input regarding the needs.
Jack Heganauer said that he had read RFP (Request for Proposal) and said that he did not think any consultant can do justice to the scope of work in a two week period for the diverse topics of the scope specifically parking since it took several weeks to get ridershop data. He said that since parking is central to the project, it deserve its own consultant. He urged Council to be careful in pushing an aggressive timeline.
Gary Martin said that he was concerned about clarifying about what is going on from public point of view, that the public does not know all the information since he only gets the staff report, that the City rushes input to meet a deadline, that the summer events season are the highest count volume, that the contract did not include analyzing the parking demand studies, request that try to encourage consultant to set realistic deadline and when the work is done that it was done right.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the consultant will be addressing questions regarding off peak traffic counts, the accuracy of the counts, the syncronization, as well as the parking issues.
Council discussed meeting the June 20th meeting date is it is ready and that the consultant will communicate his progress and need for any additional time, that the cost is being paid by the developer out of the deposit he has made to the City, that the June 14th is a goal but that it will not be submitted if it is not ready, and that the matrix was a combination of the various questions from meetings.
Eric Lodge said that May 31st is a difficult deadline for these complex issues and analysis and that the emphasis on a deadline may compromise the best product, that additional fair and race season counts should be considered when the greatest impact is felt.
Council and City Manager discussed concern about a quick deadline compromising a quality work product, that emphasis should be conveyed to the consultant regarding a qualify product and that if they need more time to ask for it rather than be restrained by a deadline, that this is a respected and qualified consultant who will be clear about the work and the time needed, and that the consultant will keep the City Manager informed and he will inform Council.
